title: Substitute EUV with nanoimprint for periodic DRAM array layers
idea: Replace EUV exposure of the repetitive storage-node-contact, landing-pad and bitline layers with jet-and-flash nanoimprint (UV-cured resist pressed by a 1x quartz template replicated from an e-beam master); keep EUV/ArF only for irregular periphery. Imprint defects are absorbed by row/column redundancy mapped to each template's defect map, and templates rotate through a replica line.
why: Fact 4 (litho capital, single EUV supplier): an imprint tool is ~1/10 the price and power of an EUV scanner; moving 3-4 of the 5-7 EUV layers could cut litho depreciation per wafer ~30-40%.

title: Substitute photoresist patterning with block-copolymer self-assembly for capacitor honeycomb
idea: Cylinder-forming PS-b-PMMA (or high-chi PS-b-PDMS) packs naturally into the same hexagonal lattice as DRAM storage nodes; a sparse ArF guide pattern (one post per 3-4 sites) registers the film and the polymer fills in the rest, then PMMA cores are removed and transferred into the hard mask. One DUV exposure plus spin-coat and 250 C bake replaces a double-EUV or SAQP hole sequence.
why: Fact 4: 3-4x density multiplication from one cheap exposure; removes 1-2 EUV layers and the hex-array LELE overlay budget.

title: Substitute 300 mm silicon wafers with Gen-8.5 display glass panels
idea: Build a capacity-tier DRAM (oxide-TFT access devices plus stacked MIM capacitors) on 2.2 x 2.5 m glass in converted LCD/OLED fabs, patterning 40-60 nm features with panel-scale nanoimprint. One panel equals the area of ~70 300 mm wafers and the line tools are largely depreciated or idle.
why: Capital intensity and U.S. manufacturability: panel fabs cost 5-10x less per m2 processed; even at 4-8x lower density than DDR5, cost per bit could compete for cold/capacity tiers. Overlay on glass and TFT leakage are the risks.

title: Substitute plasma-etched capacitor holes with self-ordered anodic alumina pores
idea: Deposit 1-2 um of aluminum over the cell transistors, pre-dimple it with a coarse DUV pattern registered to the landing pads, then anodize in oxalic acid: pores self-order into a hexagonal lattice at a pitch set by voltage (~2.5 nm/V) with AR >100:1 in minutes. Open the pore bottoms, ALD TiN/ZrO2/TiN inside, and keep the alumina as the mechanical support.
why: Facts 1 and 4: deletes the HAR etch (the slowest, costliest DRAM module) and the support-mesh patterning; AR 100-150 comes free, lifting Cs toward ~8 fF; wet anodization benches cost ~1/20 of HAR etch chambers.

title: Substitute plasma etch with metal-assisted chemical etching for vertical silicon pillars
idea: Pattern a Pt or Au catalyst mesh (lift-off or block-copolymer), then immerse the wafer in HF/H2O2: silicon under the catalyst dissolves and the mesh sinks straight down, carving vertical-channel-transistor pillars or buried-wordline trenches at >100:1 with no ion damage and no bowing; the catalyst is stripped and reclaimed.
why: Facts 2 and 4: a 50-wafer wet batch replaces $5-10M cryo/HAR etch chambers; damage-free sidewalls also shrink the GIDL leakage tail (fact 3). Metal contamination control is the main risk.

title: Substitute tungsten wordlines and contacts with chlorine-ALD molybdenum
idea: Replace WF6-based tungsten in buried wordlines, bitline contacts and periphery plugs with molybdenum deposited by ALD from MoO2Cl2, eliminating the TiN barrier and nucleation layers that fluorine chemistry demands. Mo's shorter electron mean free path gives lower resistivity than W below ~15 nm line width.
why: Scarce resource (China ~80% of W) and U.S. supply (Colorado Mo mines); 20-40% lower wordline resistance permits longer wordlines and fewer drivers, shrinking periphery (fact 7).

title: Substitute helium backside cooling with electrolyzer hydrogen and closed-loop capture
idea: Run electrostatic-chuck backside cooling in etch, CVD and implant tools with 5-20 Torr hydrogen (higher thermal conductivity than helium) from an on-site electrolyzer, and fit remaining helium uses (leak check, purge, litho) with cryogenic capture-and-reuse loops. Chuck seals get diffusion barriers so exhaust stays well under the H2 lower explosive limit.
why: Helium chokepoint (Qatar ~30%, offline since March 2026): cuts fab helium draw >80%, decoupling DRAM output from helium shocks.

title: Substitute quartz crucibles with electromagnetic cold-crucible silicon crystal growth
idea: Melt silicon in a water-cooled segmented copper crucible where induction currents push the melt off the walls (skull melting), and pull single crystals from the levitated pool under a cusp magnetic field. No fused-quartz crucible is consumed and oxygen from SiO2 dissolution disappears.
why: Removes the Spruce Pine high-purity-quartz chokepoint (>80%); oxygen-free crystals avoid oxygen precipitates that feed junction-leakage tails (fact 3).

title: Substitute sawn bulk wafers with reusable porous-silicon donor layer transfer
idea: Anodize a parent wafer to form a double porous-silicon release layer, grow 30-50 um of device-grade epitaxial silicon, bond it to a low-cost polysilicon carrier and split at the porous layer; the parent is re-polished and reused 20-50 times. DRAM front-end only needs the top few microns of single crystal.
why: Cuts ingot, polysilicon and quartz-crucible demand per DRAM wafer ~20x and lets U.S. epi reactors supply substrates.

title: Substitute periphery photomasks with maskless digital-micromirror lithography
idea: Pattern non-critical periphery layers (thick metal, implant blocks, pads, fuses) with a DMD-based maskless DUV writer, so each layer is a data file rather than a reticle; reticles are reserved for the critical array layers.
why: Fixed cost and lead time: saves ~15-20 masks per product revision, enables fast custom HBM base-die and SKU spins, and reduces reticle-shop dependency.

title: Substitute lithographic critical dimensions with sidewall-deposited film thicknesses
idea: Lay the cell on its side: gate length, channel thickness and capacitor dielectric are all set by ALD film thickness on sidewalls of coarse DUV-defined steps, so atomic-precision deposition replaces nm-precision lithography. Each tier needs only one coarse block mask because F no longer sets channel length.
why: Fact 4: breaks litho-bound scaling, since feature size follows ALD (+/-0.1 nm) instead of EUV; could remove 4-5 EUV layers per wafer.

title: Substitute robotic pick-and-place with capillary fluidic self-alignment for die bonding
idea: Dispense a water droplet on a hydrophilic bond site ringed by hydrophobic SAM; a roughly placed DRAM die (+/-50 um) is pulled into <0.5 um alignment by surface tension in milliseconds, the water evaporates, and oxide/Cu hybrid bonding follows. Precision comes from physics, so a coarse gantry can drop >10,000 dies per hour.
why: Fact 6 (HBM stacking tax): hybrid bonders run ~1-2k UPH at $3-5M each; 5-10x throughput cuts stacking capex and misalignment yield loss.

title: Substitute ion implanters with molecular monolayer doping and in-situ epitaxy
idea: Replace most of DRAM's ~20-30 implant steps with self-assembled dopant-bearing molecular monolayers (boron or phosphorus esters) that are capped and spike-annealed, plus selective in-situ-doped epitaxy for source/drain. Dose is set by the molecular footprint and coats 3D pillars that line-of-sight implants cannot reach.
why: Capital: removes many implanters and implant masks; conformal, damage-free junctions narrow the junction-leakage tail (fact 3).

title: Substitute zirconia capacitor dielectric with templated rutile titania near k=100
idea: Grow rutile-phase TiO2 (k ~80-120) by ALD at <=400 C on a RuO2 bottom electrode whose lattice templates the rutile phase, with Al doping to block leakage, so the same ~5 fF fits in a hole of AR ~25:1 instead of 70:1.
why: Facts 1 and 4: shallower holes cut HAR etch and ALD time ~3x and remove support-mesh steps (or keep AR and double Cs). Ru is itself a scarce metal and leakage is the risk.

title: Substitute litho-etch pairs with area-selective bottom-up deposition
idea: Use small-molecule or SAM inhibitors that adsorb only on dielectric so ALD grows metal (or dielectric) only where wanted, forming landing pads and capacitor bottom contacts self-aligned to underlying features without a lithography and etch pair. Selectivity loss is reset with periodic deposition-etch supercycles.
why: Removes 2-4 edge-placement-limited masks and their etch/clean steps per wafer and raises overlay yield in the dense 6F2 contacts (fact 4).

title: Substitute leading-edge EUV nodes with relaxed-pitch DUV DRAM in idle fabs
idea: Re-tool existing U.S. 300 mm mature-logic fabs to make an ~18-20 nm DRAM entirely with ArF immersion SAQP using 2018-era cell layouts, sold as capacity memory where a cost-per-bit premium is tolerable. The shell, utilities and most tools already exist.
why: Capital and time: ~18-24 months and ~$2-4B versus $15B+ and 3-5 years, with zero EUV; cost per bit ~1.5-2x worse, but adds supply into a 4x-priced market.

title: Substitute tester-based burn-in with on-die BIST and contactless wafer test
idea: Embed a programmable march/retention test engine and near-field RF coupling coils in every die so whole wafers are tested in parallel by a wafer-scale wireless tester without probe cards; weak cells are repaired by on-die eFuses during the same pass.
why: DRAM test and burn-in equipment is ~10% of capex and a throughput bottleneck; massively parallel contactless test could cut test cost ~5x and free cleanroom floor.

title: Substitute EUV projection optics with X-ray proximity printing from storage rings
idea: A compact electron storage ring feeds 12-16 soft-X-ray (~1 nm) beamlines, each exposing wafers through a 1x membrane mask held 5-10 um away; there are no mirrors to build, and the dense periodic array tolerates 1x masks written by e-beam.
why: Fact 4: ends single-supplier EUV dependence; source capital is shared across many steppers, possibly 2-3x lower cost per array layer. 1x mask distortion and cost are the risks.

title: Substitute water rinse-dry with supercritical CO2 for high-AR capacitor arrays
idea: Replace DI-water rinse and dry after capacitor mold strip with supercritical CO2 plus co-solvents, which has zero surface tension, so ultra-high-AR electrode cylinders cannot lean or stick together. This deletes the mid- and top-level nitride support meshes (two patterning steps) and allows AR >100.
why: Fact 1: pattern collapse limits capacitor AR; also cuts ultrapure-water use for these steps by a large fraction.

title: Substitute investor capital with customer-prepaid ten-year bit-supply notes
idea: Hyperscalers prepay for guaranteed exabits per year through a tradable 'bit-supply note' tied to one specific fab line, priced cost-plus with an index; the fab's capital comes from those who most fear the shortage.
why: Capital intensity: moves $15B+ of risk off the memory maker's balance sheet, shortens time-to-decision, and damps the boom-bust underinvestment behind the 4x price spike.

title: Substitute monolithic DRAM die with array wafer bonded to logic periphery
idea: Fabricate the cell array on an array-only wafer (no periphery transistors and no dual/triple gate-oxide modules, roughly half the masks) and the sense amps, decoders and I/O on a 28-16 nm logic wafer, then hybrid bond the two wafer-to-wafer at ~1 um pitch.
why: Facts 7 and 4: periphery (~49% of die) moves under the array to existing logic foundries; die area -30-40% and array-wafer process steps about -35%.

title: Substitute tin-plasma EUV sources with one shared free-electron laser
idea: A single energy-recovery-linac FEL (~10 kW at 13.5 nm) is split to feed 10-20 scanners in a DRAM fab, replacing per-scanner laser-produced tin-plasma sources that waste >99% of their drive-laser power.
why: Fact 4: abundant dose allows cheaper, faster resists and higher throughput; source capex and power per wafer could fall ~3-5x. Single point of failure is the risk.

title: Substitute ballroom cleanrooms with sealed tool-to-tool mini-environments
idea: Build the fab as a sealed transport network where pods dock tool-to-tool under nitrogen, with ISO-1 cleanliness only inside tools and AMHS tubes, so the building itself is an ordinary ISO-8 warehouse.
why: Capital: cleanroom construction, HVAC and make-up air are ~20-30% of fab capex and a major energy/water load; could cut building capex ~2/3 and build time by about a year.

title: Substitute passive silicon interposer with DRAM-filled active interposer under GPU
idea: The ~2,500 mm2 CoWoS interposer is mostly empty 65 nm-class silicon; build deep-trench-capacitor eDRAM arrays into it (deep trenches are already etched there for decoupling caps) so the GPU's hot working set sits ~50 um below the logic through hybrid bonds instead of across an HBM PHY.
why: Constraint: vertical access ~0.2-0.4 pJ/bit versus HBM 3-4 pJ/bit (>=10x); capital: reuses interposer wafer starts and trench tools already in the packaging flow, adding a few GB without TSV stacks.

title: Substitute 3 V boosted wordlines with negative-capacitance steep-slope access transistors
idea: Add a thin HZO layer to the access-transistor gate stack, capacitance-matched for negative-capacitance amplification (sub-60 mV/dec), so the same off-leakage is reached with a ~1 V wordline; the VPP charge pumps and the thick-gate-oxide periphery module with its masks are deleted.
why: Constraint and fact 10: wordline CV2 falls ~9x and ~30%-efficient pump losses vanish, giving >=10x on the row path; facet: removes 3-5 masks for dual/triple oxides.

title: Substitute room temperature with 77 K so shallow capacitors suffice
idea: Operate DRAM in liquid nitrogen, where access-transistor leakage drops >10^6, so a 0.5-1 fF capacitor with AR ~10:1 holds data for minutes; subthreshold slope steepens to ~20 mV/dec, letting array voltages fall to ~0.5 V while bitline resistance drops ~5x.
why: Constraint: 5x smaller C and 2x lower V give ~20x lower array energy per access (net ~10x after large-plant LN2 cooling overhead); facet: eliminates HAR capacitor etch and support meshes (facts 1 and 4).

title: Substitute global bitline sensing with local gain transistors from same VCT step
idea: Split each bitline into 16-cell segments; each segment's charge drives the gate of a local gain transistor made in the same vertical-channel-transistor step as the cells (no extra mask), which pulls a ~50 mV current-mode signal onto the global bitline. With a ~1 fF local line, the cell needs only ~1 fF, so the capacitor can be shallow.
why: Constraint: 50 mV global swing instead of ~0.5 V plus 5x smaller cell charge gives ~10-20x less bitline energy per access; facet: capacitor AR from ~70:1 to ~15:1 (fact 1).

title: Substitute silicon access transistors with nanoelectromechanical contact relays
idea: Each cell's access device is a sub-100 nm NEM relay (TiN cantilever over a vapor-HF-released air gap) that physically disconnects its capacitor; off-leakage is zero, so a 0.3 fF planar BEOL capacitor and a ~0.4 V pull-in design suffice, built with a 180-90 nm MEMS toolset above logic.
why: Constraint: zero leakage, tiny C and 0.4 V give >=10x lower cell and bitline energy and remove refresh; facet: no EUV, mature-node MEMS fabs. Contact wear versus unlimited endurance is the big risk.

title: Substitute sense amplifiers with complementary n-IGZO/p-SnO oxide gain cells
idea: Pair n-type IGZO and p-type SnO (or Cu2O) thin-film transistors in a 3T cell whose storage node gates a CMOS-like inverter, so a read drives a rail-to-rail level onto a short local line with no sense amplifier and no restore. Sputtered below 350 C, patterned with ArF only, stackable in BEOL.
why: Constraint: no precharge/restore and bit-granular reads remove the 128x overfetch, ~0.1-0.3 pJ per useful bit versus 5.9 pJ (>=20x); facet: DUV-only BEOL stack runnable in logic or display fabs. Poor p-oxide mobility is the risk.

title: Substitute shared row activation with dual-gate coincident-select vertical cells
idea: Give each vertical-channel access transistor two independent gates, the wordline on one face and a column-select line on the other, created by splitting the gate-all-around ring with one self-aligned spacer cut; a cell opens only where both lines are high, so only the requested 64-512 bits are sensed instead of an 8 KB row.
why: Constraint and fact 8: removes ~16-128x overfetch for ~10-30x lower energy per useful bit; facet: the added select needs no new lithography layer because the split is self-aligned.

title: Substitute bulk silicon with back-gated FD-SOI for dynamic-threshold cells
idea: Build the array on ultra-thin-body SOI with a buried back-gate plane held at deep negative bias during retention (high Vt, low leakage) and pulsed toward zero only under the activated mat, so the front wordline needs only a ~0.8 V swing; the recessed-channel BCAT etch module and VPP pumps go away.
why: Constraint: wordline energy ~14x lower (0.8 V vs 3 V) and lower bitline voltage give ~8-12x per access; facet: deletes the recessed-gate litho/etch module.

title: Substitute dissipative line charging with adiabatic resonant charge recovery
idea: Drive bitline precharge and wordlines from LC resonant rails using high-Q spiral inductors in a thick-copper redistribution layer borrowed from RF BEOL, ramping lines over ~5 ns so most of their CV2 energy returns to the tank instead of heating drivers.
why: Constraint: adiabatic recovery of 80-90% of line energy gives ~5-10x per access on the dominant line-charging term; facet: no new array lithography, only one mature thick-metal layer.

title: Substitute logic ALUs with bit-serial adders drawn from DRAM array masks
idea: Reserve every 64th mat edge for a strip of 1-bit full adders and latches built only from the array's own access transistors and capacitors as dynamic logic, on the same pitch, so no periphery masks are added; tensors are reduced bit-serially along the sense-amp row and operands never leave the mat.
why: Constraint: skips I/O and global-bus energy (most of DDR5's 10-20 pJ/bit) for >10x lower energy per elementwise or reduction operation; capital: zero new process steps.

title: Substitute hot DRAM capacity with hybrid-bonded stacks of depreciated 28 nm SRAM
idea: Stack 8-16 dies of high-density 28 nm SRAM from fully depreciated, non-EUV foundry lines directly on the accelerator by hybrid bonding as its hottest working-set tier, exploiting SRAM's non-destructive read and zero refresh.
why: Constraint: ~0.05-0.2 pJ/bit at um distance versus 3-15 pJ/bit for HBM/DDR5 (>10x); capital: no DRAM fab, no EUV. Cost per bit is ~10-20x worse, so it suits only the hottest few GB.

title: Substitute random-access cells with short-loop charge-coupled shift-register memory
idea: Store bits as charge packets in 64-stage CCD loops built only from parallel gate lines (no per-cell contacts, capacitors or access transistors), ideal for SAQP or self-assembled line/space patterning; a read clocks the loop past its single sense node using ~0.3 V three-phase clocks.
why: Constraint: a packet transfer costs ~fJ per stage, ~0.1 pJ/bit versus 5.9 pJ per useful bit; facet: line/space-only lithography, no HAR etch, 2-3 critical masks. Latency (~32-64 ns) and dark-current refresh are the risks.

title: Substitute separate memory die with DRAM built in logic wafer backside
idea: After the backside-power-delivery thinning step that 2 nm-class logic already performs, deposit an oxide-TFT plus MIM-capacitor array in the backside dielectric under the compute tiles, wired through the nano-TSVs the BSPDN flow already etches.
why: Constraint: 1-5 um vertical distance gives ~0.05-0.2 pJ/bit, >20x below HBM; capital: rides on a process step the logic fab already pays for, with no memory fab, package or TSV stack.

title: Substitute diced packaged memory with wafer-on-wafer bonding and redundancy routing
idea: Bond a whole DRAM wafer to a whole accelerator wafer without dicing, and route around defective DRAM tiles through a configurable redundancy fabric on the logic side, so no known-good-die test or per-die packaging is needed.
why: Constraint: 1-2 um bond pitch gives ~0.1 pJ/bit at TB/s per mm2 (>=30x below HBM); capital: eliminates dicing, KGD test, TSVs, interposers and substrates (fact 6).

title: Substitute high-temperature epitaxy with laser-crystallized silicon above logic
idea: Deposit amorphous silicon over finished logic BEOL and melt-crystallize it with nanosecond excimer or green laser pulses that heat only the top ~100 nm (BEOL stays below 400 C), seeding grains through small vias; then build silicon access transistors and capacitors in this layer directly over compute.
why: Constraint: memory ~1 um above logic gives ~0.1 pJ/bit access (>20x below HBM) with silicon-like leakage; capital: excimer annealers are commodity tools from LTPS display lines.

title: Substitute one-bit cells with analog charge levels and charge-domain MAC
idea: Use larger DUV-defined capacitors (~4x area, no EUV) holding 16 charge levels (4 bits) for AI weights or KV cache; on access, selected cells dump charge onto a summing line weighted by input voltages, so a whole dot product is read with one ADC conversion instead of streaming every bit out.
why: Constraint: one result moves instead of N operands, ~10-50x lower energy per MAC-equivalent access; facet: equal bit density with ~2x coarser lithography and no EUV.

title: Substitute interposer wiring with glass-core millimetre unterminated memory links
idea: Place LPDDR-class dies within 1 mm of the processor on a glass-core panel substrate with 2 um lines, and replace terminated DDR signaling with unterminated 0.2 V-swing CMOS links that behave like on-die wires; panel glass replaces silicon interposers.
why: Constraint: I/O energy falls from ~5-10 to ~0.3-0.5 pJ/bit (>=10x on the I/O share); capital: 510x515 mm glass panels cost a fraction of silicon interposers and need no TSVs.

title: Substitute copper die-to-die wires with microLED free-space optical links
idea: Each DRAM die face carries arrays of mass-transferred GaN micro-LEDs and silicon photodiodes (1-2 Gb/s per lane, thousands of lanes) that talk across the stack or to the processor through short imaging optics, replacing TSV/microbump buses and SerDes.
why: Constraint: ~0.1-0.5 pJ/bit versus 3-15 pJ/bit (>=10x); facet: no TSV etch/fill and no microbump yield loss (fact 6), using display-industry microLED transfer.

title: Substitute TSVs and microbumps with face-to-face capacitive proximity coupling
idea: Stack DRAM dies face-to-face or in a staircase so top-metal plates on neighboring dies form coupling capacitors across a ~1 um dielectric gap; data crosses as small-swing capacitive pulses with no through-silicon vias or bumps, and dies self-register with etched pits and balls.
why: Constraint: ~0.05-0.1 pJ/bit versus HBM 3-4 pJ/bit (>=30x); facet: removes TSV etch/fill/reveal and microbump steps with their 20-30% yield hit and 3x area tax (fact 6).

title: Substitute oversized cell capacitors with power-up offset-trimmed sense amplifiers
idea: Store each sense amplifier's Vt-mismatch correction in a trimmed capacitor bank calibrated at power-up, so the bitline needs only ~25 mV of signal instead of 100+ mV; cells then need ~1-1.5 fF and bitline swing can be reduced.
why: Constraint: ~4x less cell charge plus reduced swing on shorter bitlines gives ~10x lower array energy per access; facet: capacitor AR from ~70:1 to ~20:1, shrinking the HAR etch/ALD module (fact 1).

title: Substitute 77 K with 4 K quantum-paraelectric SrTiO3 planar capacitors
idea: Beside quantum computers and cryogenic accelerators, exploit SrTiO3's dielectric constant rising to ~10^4 at 4 K to make planar (AR ~1) 5 fF capacitors, with superconducting NbN bitlines and 0.2 V cryo-CMOS sensing.
why: Constraint: 0.2 V swing on lossless lines gives >=25x lower switching energy per access; facet: no HAR etch, no EUV. 4 K cooling overhead (~500-1000 W/W) means it fits only where 4 K already exists.

title: Substitute die-to-wafer bonding with micro-transfer-printed DRAM tiles on compute
idea: Release 0.5-1 mm2 DRAM tiles from their wafer by undercutting a sacrificial layer, pick thousands at once with an elastomer stamp, and print them directly over compute tiles on the processor wafer, followed by planarization and a via step for um-scale connections.
why: Constraint: tiles ~5 um above cores give ~0.1-0.3 pJ/bit access (>=10x below HBM); capital: stamps place thousands of tiles per cycle with no hybrid-bond aligner or TSVs, and tiles can come from older fabs.

title: Substitute access transistors with BEOL two-terminal selectors in line-space crosspoints
idea: Build a 1S1C crosspoint: a threshold-switching selector (NbOx or OTS) in series with a planar MIM capacitor at each intersection of two perpendicular line arrays, which need only line/space patterning (SAQP or DSA, no contact holes, no EUV) and stack in BEOL; only the single selected intersection is charged or read.
why: Constraint: bit-granular access on short 4F2 lines gives ~0.2-0.5 pJ per useful bit versus 5.9 pJ (>=10x); facet: ~3 masks per layer, BEOL-stackable. Selector leakage forces frequent refresh.
